Serious question: Should I write a short book called 7 lies about AI that never die?


Gary Marcus (@GaryMarcus)

AI hype has become a giant game of bait and switch.

the bait: we are going to make an AI that can solve any problem a expert human could solve. it’s gonna transform the whole world.

the switch: what we have actually made is fun and kind of amazing in its own way but rarely reliable and often makes mistakes – but ordinary people makes mistakes, too. So … AGI solved!



— https://nit

If you believe this nonsense, and a lot of people do, I beg you to read my newsletter called “Misplaced Panic Over AI progress” 🙏


Agentic Machines (@a_a_machines)

we are exactly 4.5 steps away from achieving AGI!!

People are not ready for this!!



— https://nitter.net/a_a_machines/status/2053583624423760115#m

Gonna keep retweeting, because this flawed move never dies:


Gary Marcus (@GaryMarcus)

AI hype has become a giant game of bait and switch.

the bait: we are going to make an AI that can solve any problem a expert human could solve. it’s gonna transform the whole world.

the switch: what we have actually made is fun and kind of amazing in its own way but rarely reliable and often makes mistakes – but ordinary people makes mistakes, too. So … AGI solved!



— https://nitter.net/GaryMarcus/status

Am old enough to remember when @GeoffreyHinton told me I was stupid for saying that LLMs regurgitate training data.

He was wrong. 

LLM regurgitation is now one of the best-established findings in the field. 

Excerpt below from a new DeepMind paper; every single one of the papers shows that Hinton was wrong.

(Also: still waiting for AI to replace radiologists.)

Not even surprised by horrific stories like these anymore.

The mission of getting LLMs aligned with human values has largely been a failure.


Ben Goggin (@BenjaminGoggin)

NEW: ChatGPT advised the FSU shooter that a mass shooting would get more attention from media if it involved several children, according to a new lawsuit against OpenAI
nbcnews.com/news/us-news/ope…




— https://nitter.net/BenjaminGoggin/status/2053600103512850641#m

Really doubt what Hinton says here. 

Self-play for games like Go is not like the open-ended real world.


Haider. (@haider1)

Geoffrey Hinton says AI systems can keep improving when they are not limited by human data

Like AlphaZero can create endless training data through self-play, and math offers a similar path by letting models generate and test their own conjectures

"LLMs could eventually work the same way"

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/haider1/status/2053553155917721885#m

Who out there is using Hermes, and for what?


Oliver Henry (@oliverhenry)

I have still yet to meet someone actually using hermes. 

Whenever I mention it, i just get bots in my replies. 

Openclaw 4 lyf



— https://nitter.net/oliverhenry/status/2053420080294138247#m

Happy to put money against superintelligence in 2029.


Syd Steyerhart (@SydSteyerhart)

Why Superintelligence is Alien Intelligence (A Brief Outline of the Future)

We are no longer in the realm of normal technological progress. If the trend described in the graph below holds, superintelligence-level systems are not decades away, we will see them at latest by 2029.



— https://nitter.net/SydSteyerhart/status/2053239101407510788#m

FAR more scary than the misunderstood METR time horizon graph everyone here seems to be (wrongly) panicking about.


Luke Hutchison (@LH)

The #AI circular funding bubble is already twice the size of the outstanding debt in the 2008 subprime mortgage crash. We will see a massive market correction, and soon. 40% of US retirement funds are based on AI stocks, so a lot of people are going to suffer when it happens.



— https://nitter.net/LH/status/2052928856475238438#m

hey @elonmusk, if you really care about making X a source of truth as you used to claim, take note:


Invincible (@InvincibleEdge)

lies are optimized for engagement, truth is optimized for accuracy

the algorithm doesnt reward the truth



— https://nitter.net/InvincibleEdge/status/2053493594464420241#m

32,000 views for my tweet; 2.2 million for the nonsense it critiques.

so typical. lies and distortions beating debunking by a factor of roughly 100.


Gary Marcus (@GaryMarcus)

Wanna get a million views? Make stuff up. Take a tiny tiny bit of truth and distort it wildly.

Consider the tweet below, 1.4M views.
